subject: Eval alignment & next steps: retrieval sweep + reranker A/B for Lumena POC
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@lumenahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Eval alignment & next steps: retrieval sweep + reranker A/B for Lumena POC

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of actions so we can convert the POC into a short evaluation sprint: 

Summary of where we landed
- Target UX: in-app question answering for medical records + clinician notes (short form Q&A + long-form summaries).
- Key risk: hallucination on out-of-context references and sensitivity to small prompt changes.
- Success signals you mentioned: grounding recall (documents referenced correctly), answer helpfulness (clinician-rated), and low hallucination rate.

Proposed evaluation plan (short):
1) Retrieval sweep — run three configs from the same dataset:  
   - Config A: dense embeddings (OpenEmbed-2) + top_k=10 + chunk_size=512
   - Config B: dense embeddings + top_k=20 + chunk_size=256 (more recall)
   - Config C: hybrid BM25 + dense rerank (top_k=100 candidate, dense re-rank k=20)
2) Reranker A/B — test two reranker approaches post-retrieval:  
   - Reranker X: cross-encoder cross-attention reranker (higher precision, heavier)
   - Reranker Y: bi-encoder re-score + light logistic combiner (faster, cheaper)
3) Model mix for generation — evaluate both Llama-2-13b-chat (full-res) and a quantized Redwood-optimized-7B (q4) for latency/cost tradeoffs.
4) Prompt sets & eval metrics — we attached a first-pass prompt set (lumena_rag_eval_promptset_v1.json). Key metrics: grounding recall (target >= 0.92), hallucination rate (allowed <= 2%), clinician helpfulness (mean >= 4.0/5), latency p95 <= 800ms for common queries.

Deliverables we will share by Tuesday: retrieval_sweep_config.yaml (exact commands + parameter grid), a link to the baseline benchmark run, and the prompt set. Can you confirm: 1) the sample dataset location (S3 path) we should use, and 2) a point person on your side for running the lightweight client tests?

Thanks — I’ll pair Monica on the reranker config and she’ll own the benchmark automation.

Best,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: lumena_rag_eval_promptset_v1.json (prompt set, 120 prompts), retrieval_sweep_config.yaml (sweep grid)

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@lumenahealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumena Health - POC Team <poc@lumenahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval alignment & next steps: retrieval sweep + reranker A/B for Lumena POC

Nikhil —

Appreciate the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications before we kick off: 

- Dataset: we will share a sanitized S3 path by EOD today: s3://lumena-poc/samples/aug2026. Use the de-identified_ set (we excluded PHI).
- Point person: that will be me for the first run; I’ll have our infra lead (poc@lumenahealth.com) stand by for credential handoff.

On metrics: the thresholds look reasonable, though clinician helpfulness target at 4.0 is ambitious — we can aim for 3.8 as a ramp target. Also curious: do you have a recommended evaluation harness to compute hallucination rate and grounding recall?

Finally, could you add a small smoke test that asserts no PII leakage for the sampled queries? We need that check in the first run.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Sr. Product Manager — Knowledge & Search, Lumena Health

On a side note: if the cross-encoder shows a material lift on grounding recall, we may be ok with higher latency for clinician workflows but would prefer a fallback low-latency path for chatbots in patient-facing flows.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@lumenahealth.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval alignment & next steps: retrieval sweep + reranker A/B for Lumena POC

Thanks Elaine — will do. Couple of practical notes we’ll include in the sweep config: 

- Evaluation harness: we’ll provide a small PyTest-compatible runner that computes: grounding_recall (document-level overlap), hallucination_rate (asserts presence of unsupported facts), exact_match for short Qs, and an annotator UI export for clinician ratings. Link to runner: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_benchmarks (attached baseline_benchmarks_link.txt in the email).
- PII smoke test: added. It’s a regex-based check plus a second pass with a lightweight NER model to flag anything that looks like PHI. We’ll fail the run if flagged items > 0 and return the example indices.
- Resource note: cross-encoder reranker (Reranker X) will need GPU-backed instances for the offline batch re-rank stage; we’ll include cost estimates in the YAML.

Next steps I’ll own: update retrieval_sweep_config.yaml with the three configs, add exact invocation examples, and push the initial benchmark run to the shared drive. Expected ETA: Monday EOD (we’ll try to accelerate to Monday morning).

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@lumenahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval alignment & next steps: retrieval sweep + reranker A/B for Lumena POC

Elaine —

Great — thanks for confirming. Quick follow-ups and the concrete asks for the first run (so we don’t block):

1) Please share the S3 path and IAM read-only role or temporary creds (we can accept a short-term pre-signed URL if you prefer).
2) Approve the attached sweep grid (we attached retrieval_sweep_config.yaml) or tell us which param to tweak. Our recommended starting point: run Config A and C in parallel, and run Reranker X only on the top candidate set for Config C to save compute.
3) Confirm the clinician rating cadence — do you want a 20-sample stratified set per config for annotation, or can we start with 10 samples each to accelerate the first pass?

Operational notes:
- If cross-encoder cost is a blocker, we will propose a two-stage approach (bi-encoder prefilter -> small cross-encoder only on top-20 candidates).
- We’ll flag any quality regressions vs your baseline automatically and post them to the Drive folder with diffs and example prompts that trigger regressions.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow morning to review the sweep YAML and confirm the credential exchange. Grace is looping in on SLA/capacity questions if we need to provision dedicated capacity for the re-rank runs.

Best,
Nikhil
